policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος and τὸν ὄφιν τὸν ἀρχαῖον differ only in case, nominative apposition against accusative agreement with τὸν δράκοντα, and ASV 'the dragon, the old serpent' is identical under either.
ASV reads 'which is the Devil and Satan, and bound him' with nothing answering RP's added ὁ πλανῶν τὴν οἰκουμένην ὅλην, so the shorter text is what it rendered.
πλανήσῃ and πλανᾷ are aorist and present of the same verb in the same ἵνα μή clause, and ASV 'that he should deceive the nations no more' does not show the aspect.

ASV renders every καί in this verse ('and cast', 'and shut', 'and sealed'), but joins μετὰ ταῦτα with a colon and no conjunction — 'should be finished: after this he must be loosed' — so the text lacked RP's καὶ before μετά.
λυθῆναι αὐτὸν and αὐτὸν λυθῆναι differ only in order, and ASV 'he must be loosed' is identical under either.
ASV writes 'reigned with Christ a thousand years' here while rendering the articular τὰ χίλια ἔτη of verses 3 and 5 as 'the thousand years', so the indefinite article reflects anarthrous χίλια.
ASV opens every other verse of this chapter with 'And' for verse-initial καί, but begins verse 5 'The rest of the dead', so its text had no καί before οἱ λοιποί.
ASV reads 'reign with him a thousand years' and footnotes 'Some ancient authorities read the', an explicit mapped note placing the article τὰ in the margin and anarthrous χίλια in the text.
The variant is only whether Μαγώγ also carries τόν, and 'Gog and Magog' renders the proper names without articles under either reading.

ASV's relative 'the number of whom is as the sand of the sea' renders ὧν ὁ ἀριθμὸς idiomatically without a separate word for the resumptive αὐτῶν, so its presence or absence leaves the English unchanged.
ἐκύκλευσαν and ἐκύκλωσαν are alternative aorists of the same verb, both rendered 'compassed'.
ASV reads 'fire came down out of heaven' and footnotes 'Some ancient authorities insert from God', an explicit mapped note keeping ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ out of the text it rendered.
ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῦ, ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν, and ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ all give 'him that sat upon it'.
The variant is only the article on προσώπου, and ASV's 'from whose face' is identical whether or not τοῦ stands.
θάνατος ὁ δεύτερός and δεύτερός θάνατος differ only in order and article placement; both are 'the second death'.
τῇ βίβλῳ and τῷ βιβλίῳ are the feminine and neuter nouns for the same object, both rendered 'the book of life'.
